interface.equation: ∂t f + v ∂x f − κ x ∂v f = ∂v(vf) + ∂v² f on R²
interface.parameter_range: 0 < κ < 1/4; unit friction and unit temperature
interface.entropy: H(f|Fκ)=∫ f log(f/Fκ) dx dv for normalized probability densities

claims.claim: The exact mean-zero L² spectral gap and sharp semigroup exponent are ακ=(1−sqrt(1−4κ))/2.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed 0<κ<1/4, the generator spectrum on mean-zero L²(Fκ) is {−j ακ−k βκ : j,k∈N₀, j+k≥1}, βκ=1−ακ.
claims.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt: Gaussian rescaling and invariant Wiener-chaos decomposition; first-chaos eigenvalue gives sharpness.

claims.claim: No positive L² or relative-entropy decay exponent is uniform over 0<κ≤κ₀ for any κ₀>0.
claims.quantifiers: There do not exist C<∞ and λ>0 independent of κ such that the stated bound holds for all t≥0 and all mean-zero L² data, or for all normalized finite-entropy densities.
claims.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt: the slow eigenfunction and the covariance-preserving shifted Gaussian have exact exponents ακ and 2ακ; ακ~κ.

claims.claim: A uniform L² rate is restored on compact parameter intervals 0<κ_*≤κ≤κ^*<1/4.
claims.quantifiers: There exists K(κ_*,κ^*)<∞ such that for every κ in the interval, every t≥0, and every mean-zero g, ||P_tκ g||₂≤K exp(−α(κ_*)t)||g||₂.
claims.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt: normalized drift eigenvectors remain uniformly conditioned on the compact interval.

claims.claim: Arnold–Erb's sharp entropy theorem at ν=σ=1 and V=κx²/2 yields the exact parameterwise entropy exponent 2ακ, and their sharpness result matches it.
claims.quantifiers: For each 0<κ<1/4, the Theorem 4.9 hypotheses hold and its finite-entropy estimate applies; Theorem 6.1 establishes sharpness.

falsifier.test: For any proposed uniform λ>0 choose κ with 2ακ<λ; the claimed inequality would force exp((λ−2ακ)t)≤C for all t, impossible as t→∞.

primary_sources.title: Sharp entropy decay for hypocoercive and non-symmetric Fokker–Planck equations with linear drift

primary_sources.authors: Jean Dolbeault, Clément Mouhot, Christian Schmeiser
primary_sources.title: Hypocoercivity for linear kinetic equations conserving mass
primary_sources.comparison: Micro–macro assumptions expose the position Poincaré constant Λ=κ and unit velocity gap λ_m=1; no uniform bound follows as κ↓0.

unresolved: No claim is made for all weakly confining nonquadratic potentials or bounded domains.
No new theorem or historical novelty is claimed.
